claims.subject: Barcelona; Athens
claims.text: The Acropolis, located in Athens, Greece, is open to visitors from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily. The ticket price for adults is €20, while children under 18 years old can enter for free. The museum is closed on January 1 and December 25.

references.label: P1.1
references.text: Barcelona[a] is a city on the northeastern coast of Spain.

references.label: P1.2
references.text: It is the capital and largest city of the autonomous community of Catalonia, as well as the second-most populous municipality of Spain after Madrid.

references.label: P1.3
references.text: With a population of 1.7 million within city limits,[3] its urban area extends to numerous neighbouring municipalities within the province of Barcelona and is home to around 5.7 million people,[4] making it the fifth most populous urban area of the European Union after Paris, the Ruhr area, Madrid, and Milan.[4] It is one of the largest metropolises on the Mediterranean Sea, located on the coast between the mouths of the rivers Llobregat and Besòs, and bounded to the west by the Serra de Collserola mountain range.

references.label: P4.1
references.text: Athens[a] is the capital and largest city of Greece.

references.label: P4.2
references.text: A significant coastal urban area in the Mediterranean, Athens is also the capital of the Attica region and is the southernmost capital on the European mainland.

references.label: P4.3
references.text: With its urban area's population numbering over 3.6 million, it is the eighth-largest urban area in the European Union (EU).

references.label: P4.4
references.text: The Municipality of Athens (also City of Athens), which constitutes a small administrative unit of the entire urban area, had a population of 643,452 in 2021,[4] within its official limits, and a land area of 38.96 square kilometres (15.04 square miles).[7][8] Athens joined the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities in 2016.
